description: Harden the Express backend for production: env-based config, security middleware, rate limiting, input validation, health check, graceful shutdown, error handling, and updated .gitignore
steps: At the top of /projects/sandbox/anotnigeia/server/index.js, add require('dotenv').config() as the first line before other imports
Replace hardcoded JWT_SECRET with process.env.JWT_SECRET || 'cryptomine-secret-key-2026' (fallback for dev only, log a warning if env var is missing)
Replace app.use(cors()) with configurable CORS: app.use(cors({ origin: process.env.CORS_ORIGIN || '*', credentials: true }))
Add require('helmet') and app.use(helmet()) before other middleware
Add express-rate-limit: create a general limiter (100 requests per 15 minutes) and a strict auth limiter (10 requests per 15 minutes) for /api/auth/ routes
Add input validation: validate phone as digits-only 9+ chars in register, sanitize comment text (trim, max 500 chars) in blog post, validate account string in set-account
Add GET /health endpoint that returns { status: 'ok', timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), uptime: process.uptime() }

Add a global error handler middleware at the bottom (after all routes) that catches unhandled errors and returns 500 with { error: 'Internal server error' } in production or the error message in development
Add graceful shutdown handlers for SIGTERM and SIGINT that close the database connection and exit cleanly
Update /projects/sandbox/anotnigeia/.gitignore to add entries for server/cryptomine.db-shm, server/cryptomine.db-wal, server/.env, and ensure server/cryptomine.db is already covered
Add a Procfile at /projects/sandbox/anotnigeia/server/Procfile with: web: node index.js
Add a brief comment block near the DB initialization noting that SQLite requires persistent filesystem storage in production (not ephemeral containers)
acceptance_criteria: node --check /projects/sandbox/anotnigeia/server/index.js passes with no syntax errors
JWT_SECRET is read from process.env with a dev fallback
CORS origin is configurable via CORS_ORIGIN env var
helmet middleware is applied before routes
Rate limiting is applied globally and with stricter limits on /api/auth routes
Global error handler middleware exists after routes
Procfile exists with web process defined
